why: The pips arm draws only the stocks remaining (issue #230), so a lost stock leaves no hollow pip behind and the pip that just emptied has nowhere to be drawn. That removes the arm's permanent channel -- shape saying how many are gone -- and leaves a shrinking row that reads like a count going down rather than a stock being knocked out.
killedBy: hud: stock-loss cue arms (issue #230) pips: one pip per starting stock, lost ones hollow, and the one just lost carries the cue
